races.name: Coral Rewards Shaker Handicap Stakes (Gbbplus Race)

runners_data.name: Tierra Del Toro
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner for Ralph Beckett and James Doyle; course form is modest on this evidence (9th at Goodwood over 12f last time) and the step up to 1m4f for the first time stretches stamina queries — the style fit note signals it may be racing slightly out of its most effective role.|
runners_data.comment: Tierra Del Toro has been in the frame in four of his last five starts, including a win four starts back. Rated 104 and the top-rated of nine, the only blot is a below-par ninth last time out.

runners_data.name: Cannes
runners_data.note: Joseph O'Brien's runner arrives 41 days fresh with a clear recent win over this course and distance at Goodwood (1/12f/GOO), prominent style suits the expected race shape, and Dylan Browne McMonagle's big-race experience is an asset on a track that rewards intelligent front-rank riding.|
runners_data.comment: A winner two starts back and runner-up in the two starts before that, this colt was unplaced last time out. The yard is firing at 28% over the last fortnight, and that flop is the one query.

runners_data.name: Infraad
runners_data.note: William Haggas's 3yo is lightly raced with honest recent form including a win at this course over 10f; prominent style fits the anticipated race shape well, Tom Marquand keeps the ride, and the step up from 10f to 12f looks a logical progression.|
runners_data.comment: Infraad has been placed in all four of his recent starts, winning two starts back and finishing third last time out, and has raced over today's going before. Rated 94 and ranked fourth of nine, he's yet to add to that success since.

runners_data.name: Bay Royale
runners_data.note: Harry Eustace's gelding won over 10f on good at Goodwood and carries cheekpieces (hg:t), suggesting he needs some encouragement to show his best; the 71-day absence is the key flag, though the positive Goodwood record and prominent style mean he cannot be dismissed if fit.|
runners_data.comment: Bay Royale won two starts back and was runner-up last time out, since when he's had a lengthy 71-day break, with a fourth three starts back the only blot. Rated 86 and ranked seventh of nine, that lay-off is the concern.

runners_data.name: Hatteen
runners_data.note: Andrew Balding's hold-up performer has strong recent Goodwood form including a 1m4f win here, making him the most course-proven of the hold-up types; Oisin Murphy will likely stalk from off the pace and needs the prominent bunch to set an honest gallop to deliver a meaningful challenge.|
runners_data.comment: Hatteen won last time out and was runner-up in the two starts before that, with his trainer firing at 26% over the last fortnight. Rated 83, he's only eighth of nine on our figures despite that recent upturn.

runners_data.name: Baltic Fleet
runners_data.note: Ian Williams's 3yo is a natural prominent racer whose true style cannot be replicated in a field this saturated with forward-going types; the 61-day absence adds uncertainty, and William Buick will need to improvise a position that doesn't suit this horse's optimal profile.|
runners_data.comment: Baltic Fleet was runner-up last time out and has been placed in four of his last five starts, including a win four starts back. Rated 94 and ranked third of nine, the main concern is a 61-day break since he last ran.

runners_data.name: Blue Hercules
runners_data.note: Muir & Grassick's runner has solid course form including a recent 2nd over 12f at Goodwood but holds five runs on this going without a win; holds up in running, will need the pace to be genuinely strong and a clear run through, both of which are uncertain given the prominent-heavy field.|
runners_data.comment: Blue Hercules is winless in his last five starts but was runner-up last time out and three starts back, with an unplaced effort and a below-par eighth further back. Rated 88 and ranked sixth of nine, he's up against it without that breakthrough win.

runners_data.name: Parisian Scholar
runners_data.note: Charlie Johnston's 3yo is on a good run with back-to-back wins over this course and distance; hold-up style means it depends on others doing the donkey work, but the Goodwood-specific form record (2W in last 5 at this track/trip) is a genuine positive for Rowan Scott.|
runners_data.comment: Parisian Scholar has won his last two starts on the bounce, having previously managed only a fourth, an unplaced effort and a seventh. Rated 92 and ranked fifth of nine, that recent upturn is the headline, though his form before it was modest.

runners_data.name: Sea And Sun
runners_data.note: Second Johnston runner with limited form (three runs, form 224) and an unknown style classification; the 20-day turnaround is fine, soft-ground form suggests it handles cut, and all three career runs have been over 11-12f, so the trip is established — but the modest OR of 80 and unknown tactical profile make this an outsider.|
runners_data.comment: Sea And Sun is winless in his last three starts but was runner-up in two of them, including two starts back, before a fourth last time out. Rated 82 and bottom of nine on our figures, he needs more to be competitive here.

races.paceDynamic: Tierra Del Toro is the confirmed front-runner here, with Cannes, Infraad, Bay Royale, and Baltic Fleet all carrying prominent profiles — meaning the field is saturated with horses wanting to race close to the pace. Tierra Del Toro will set the tempo on good ground over this 1m4f trip at Goodwood, but with multiple horses pressing to sit just behind, the pace should be honest and sustained rather than artificially slow. Baltic Fleet is a genuine prominent type who cannot realistically secure that forward position in this shape and has been mapped to midfield, which is not its natural home. This race shape — a consistent, uncontested gallop from Tierra Del Toro with a competitive group tracking just off the pace — should theoretically suit hold-up horses finishing through beaten rivals, but the redistribution of prominent types like Baltic Fleet into deeper ground means the most natural beneficiaries are those who can travel fluently in the first four and pick up off the strong pace, making prominent-to-midfield racers with proven Goodwood form the primary profile to follow.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Honest Pace, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Tierra Del Toro sets a genuine gallop and the prominent pack tracks efficiently, allowing the strongest traveller to quicken off the pace.
scenarios.body: The steady but unrelenting fractions suit horses sitting just off the lead who can sustain their effort through Goodwood's undulations; the lack of a late sprint premium rewards class and stamina over pure acceleration.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Closers Reel Them In
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent pack burns faster fractions than anticipated through the middle of the race, leaving them vulnerable to hold-up horses finishing powerfully.
scenarios.body: The compressed field and crowded prominent section creates a faster early pace that sets up a strong late run from further back; horses with tactical patience benefit most in this scenario.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front Runner Sticks
scenarios.trigger: If Tierra Del Toro dictates at a controlled tempo and the chasing pack fails to mount a coordinated challenge, leaving the lead horse in front longer than expected.
scenarios.body: A slow-burn gallop on good ground at Goodwood can neutralise hold-up horses entirely if the sectionals never compress; Tierra Del Toro's course form and James Doyle's tactical nous make this a genuine possibility.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Midfield Chaos, Unexpected Winner
scenarios.trigger: If Baltic Fleet and other redistributed types fail to settle in unnatural positions, creating shuffling and interference that disrupts the expected race shape entirely.
scenarios.body: Disrupted fracking through the field scrambles the tactical picture and can produce a winner from an unlikely position; horses with relaxed temperaments and clean runs benefit disproportionately.

watchPoints.text: Cannes and Infraad are both prominent types with Goodwood course wins and strong connections — watch which settles more comfortably in the early stages, as the one travelling better at halfway is likely to feature prominently in the finish.

Baltic Fleet cannot realistically claim its natural forward position in this field; watch whether William Buick drops it in behind early or fights for position, as either choice carries tactical risk and could affect those immediately around it.

Bay Royale has not run for 71 days and wears cheekpieces — first-time headgear effects on a horse returning from a break can be unpredictable, and Pierre-Louis Jamin will need to manage early exuberance carefully.

Hatteen's Goodwood 1m4f win is the standout course-and-distance qualifier among the hold-up horses — if the pace is strong enough from the front, Oisin Murphy's positioning off the pace could bring him into the finish faster than the market implies.

Parisian Scholar has won twice over this exact course and distance recently — Rowan Scott's rides here have been quietly effective and the booking for a Charlie Johnston improver on form deserves monitoring in the betting market.

races.name: British Stallion Studs Ebf Alice Keppel Fillies' Conditions Stakes (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Call Nicki
runners_data.note: Six career runs at Goodwood with two wins, all on similar going — a pattern of relentless course form under David Allan that marks her out as the hardest horse to dislodge from the front; the question is whether Fast Track's presence beside her costs enough energy to let a stalker land a late blow.
runners_data.comment: Call Nicki won her last two starts back-to-back and has been placed in five of her last six. Ranked bottom of nine at 78 despite that form, she faces a stiff task on our figures alone.

runners_data.name: Divine Whisper
runners_data.note: George Boughey's filly has a perfect 1-2 record at Goodwood on good ground and Billy Loughnane rides; she is a natural prominent racer but with the lead slots already heavily populated, she is likely to find herself further back than ideal and her chance must be tempered accordingly.
runners_data.comment: Two starts have brought a runner-up effort and a win last time out for Divine Whisper, who has also run over today's trip and going before. Lightly raced with just two starts to date, she sits seventh of nine at 81 on our figures.

runners_data.name: Envision
runners_data.note: James Owen's charge broke her maiden at Goodwood but posted a 22nd in her most recent start here, raising questions about consistency; she sits in the pace map further back than her instincts would dictate — a true front-of-group type squeezed rearward — so treat her chance with caution unless she secures better early position than the congestion allows.
runners_data.comment: A winner two starts back after a fourth before that, this filly was unplaced last time out and ranks eighth of nine on our figures. Her yard is in good heart at 36% over the last fortnight, but she needs to bounce back.

runners_data.name: Fast Track
runners_data.note: A course-and-distance winner wearing a tongue-tie, trained in-form by Andrew Balding and ridden by Oisin Murphy — the strongest credentials among the leads; her one poor run (14th) was sandwiched between placed efforts, suggesting she handles the track, and Murphy will seek to settle the front-running argument quickly.
runners_data.comment: Fast Track bounced back to win last time out after an unplaced run two starts back, with her trainer firing at a 26% strike rate over the last fortnight. Rated 96 and ranked second of nine, that blank two back is the only blip.

runners_data.name: Hidden Gift
runners_data.note: OR=120 stands out as the highest-rated runner in the field though her two-run record over this trip is modest (5th, 2nd); Oisin Orr takes over in the prominent pack and if she is as good as her rating implies she could make a bold move, but the rating gap from her form reads as unexplained potential rather than proven class.
runners_data.comment: Hidden Gift finished fifth last time out having been runner-up the run before, and remains winless in her last two starts. Her trainer is out of form at just 5% over the last fortnight, adding to the concerns at a rating of 85, fifth of nine.

runners_data.name: Miss Lizzy
runners_data.note: Charlie Fellowes' filly wears a tongue-tie and has shown glimpses of ability including a six-furlong win at Sandown, but her Goodwood record is patchy with a 1-1-1 record in runs here counting only one placed effort; Paddy Bradley takes the ride and she will need to find a clear passage from mid-pack.
runners_data.comment: Miss Lizzy was third last time out and a winner four starts back, though results in between have been mixed with an unplaced run and a fifth. Rated 90 and ranked third of nine, she has claims on her best form but needs more consistency.

runners_data.name: Princesse d'Orange
runners_data.note: Ryan Moore is the significant booking for David O'Meara but Princesse d'Orange has yet to win on good ground at Goodwood, recording a 17th last time here; her 1530 form suggests she can threaten but has not yet translated talent into a win at this track on this surface.
runners_data.comment: Princesse d'Orange won four starts back but has since faded, finishing fifth, third and then unplaced last time out. Rated 86 and ranked fourth of nine, bouncing back from that below-par run is the main question.

runners_data.name: Wild Blossom
runners_data.note: Lightly raced — just two starts — with a course-and-distance win last time under James Doyle for K.R. Burke; the unknown angle is whether a 42-day absence and limited experience allows her to handle a competitive, congested race shape, though her physical profile (OR=98) suggests there is upside if she handles the occasion.
runners_data.comment: Wild Blossom won two starts back and has run over today's trip and going before, with her trainer in strong form at 34% over the last fortnight. Rated 101, the top-rated of nine, the only concern is a blank effort last time out.

runners_data.name: Zigazig Ah
runners_data.note: Richard Spencer's filly arrives on the back of back-to-back wins, most recently at Goodwood, and Saffie Osborne retains the ride; with a 2W-2P record on similar going and only 11 days since her last run, her freshness and recent winning momentum make her one of the most dangerous prominent types in the field if she can slot into the right position behind the two front-runners.
runners_data.comment: A pair of wins in her last two starts puts Zigazig Ah in good form, having been runner-up before that, and she has run over today's trip before. Rated 83 and ranked sixth of nine, she's quick to return just 11 days on from her last outing.

races.paceDynamic: Call Nicki and Fast Track are confirmed front-runners who will clash for the lead from the off, creating a genuinely contested early pace over Goodwood's straight five furlongs on good ground. With four of nine runners wanting a prominent position, there will be pressure and congestion two to three furlongs out as Zigazig Ah, Miss Lizzy, Princesse d'Orange, and Hidden Gift all attempt to track the leaders through a compressed midfield. The field holds more front-running and prominent types than the race can accommodate cleanly — Call Nicki and Fast Track are most likely to actually secure the lead, with Zigazig Ah best placed to take the next berth given her recent winning form, while Divine Whisper and Envision are displaced rearward from their natural positions. An honest, competitively-set pace in a straight sprint on good ground historically benefits horses who can race with cover in a prominent-to-midfield position and sustain their effort to the line — true closers will find it harder to make ground from a disadvantaged draw in a field that burns off quickly.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Contested Pace, Prominent Stays On
scenarios.trigger: If Call Nicki and Fast Track fight for the lead at a strong clip, leaving the door open for a stalker to pick up the pieces inside the final furlong.
scenarios.body: The duel between the two leaders burns both slightly, allowing a well-positioned prominent runner sitting a length or two back to swoop with a clean run in the final 100 yards; on a flat, straight course with good ground, the finishing effort is sustained rather than spectacular.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Dictates and Holds
scenarios.trigger: If one of the two leads takes a decisive advantage at the break and the other fails to match early strides, allowing a solo lead to be established.
scenarios.body: The solo leader — most likely Fast Track given Oisin Murphy's tactical awareness — dictates a controlled gallop and kicks again inside the final furlong, proving too strong for the prominent trackers; OR=86 and a course win underpin the case.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Finisher Swoops Through
scenarios.trigger: If the pace genuinely collapses the leaders and the field fans wide, creating a clear late lane for a hold-up type to motor through.
scenarios.body: Wild Blossom, whose single course win came with a strong late effort, would be the primary beneficiary if she is allowed to build momentum from a midfield position; however this scenario is tempered by the field's lack of genuine hold-up types — Divine Whisper and Envision are naturally prominent and less likely to deliver a true late burst from the rear.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Fizzles, Tactical Race
scenarios.trigger: If the two leaders eyeball each other so early that the pace paradoxically collapses after the first furlong, reducing the race to a two-furlong sprint.
scenarios.body: Horses with a sharp turn of foot and prominent position — Princesse d'Orange (Ryan Moore) or Hidden Gift — could capitalise if the race turns tactical and finishes in a rush; neither has the strongest recent form but both carry top pilots capable of manufacturing a run.

watchPoints.text: Call Nicki and Fast Track will both be asked for the lead immediately — watch for a bumping or crowding incident at the break that could unsettle either runner and compromise their rhythm over only five furlongs.

Four runners (Zigazig Ah, Miss Lizzy, Princesse d'Orange, Hidden Gift) will attempt to hold a prominent position simultaneously — significant traffic danger two to three furlongs out as the field compresses and runners are forced to switch or check.

Divine Whisper is a natural prominent racer who is likely to find herself trapped further back than ideal; if Billy Loughnane attempts to push forward and reclaim a front-rank position, she risks overcooking her race in a small nine-runner field.

Wild Blossom is lightly raced with only two career starts — watch for signs of inexperience in the pre-race or during the early stages of what will be a notably busier tactical environment than her debut win suggested.

Envision's most recent run produced a finishing position of 22nd at Goodwood — a significant red flag on a course she has also won at; monitor her behaviour in the stalls and whether Cieren Fallon elects to push up early or accepts a compromised position.

races.name: Rolls-royce Oak Tree Stakes (Group 3)

runners_data.name: Flora Of Bermuda
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner and dual course-and-distance winner, but her last five runs have all been over 6f and stepping to 7f here is an unresolved stamina question — if the extra furlong finds her out, her lead evaporates in the final 100 yards; style fit is solid but trip concern is real.
runners_data.comment: A winner last time out, and again three starts back, with two victories in its last five starts to boost claims. Already raced over today's trip and going, and rated the form pick of this field, with a couple of below-par runs clouding the picture.

runners_data.name: Royal Velvet
runners_data.note: William Buick takes over on a mare who has won twice over this exact course and trip in her last five starts and goes exceptionally well on Good ground at Goodwood — strong prominent profile, high sim-going strike rate, and a trainer in form; the key profile horse for this race shape.
runners_data.comment: Fifth last time out but has two wins in its last five starts, so retains ability on her day. Has run over today's trip and going before, leaving her something to prove back in this company.

runners_data.name: Brazilian Rose
runners_data.note: A hold-up type from Rebecca Menzies's northern yard with a headgear flag, she has shown ability over this trip but her sim-going record is thin (3/15) and she is a 250-1 outsider stepping into Group 3 company for the first time over course; very much one for the each-way margins.
runners_data.comment: One win in its last six starts, and a well-beaten ninth last time out, don't inspire much confidence. Has run over today's trip and going before, but sits at the foot of these ratings with a lot to find.

runners_data.name: Dash Of Azure
runners_data.note: Ralph Beckett has runners firing at a healthy rate and Hector Crouch partners a mare who has placed twice at Goodwood already this season over 7f — naturally prominent, strong Goodwood form, and her two-from-two placed record at the track over course and distance makes her highly relevant here.
runners_data.comment: Runner-up in each of her last two starts, form strong enough to see her rated fourth in this field. Still without a win in her last five starts, but those placed efforts make her a leading threat here.

runners_data.name: Havana Pusey
runners_data.note: A hold-up specialist with genuine course knowledge — three wins in five Good-ground starts over this trip at Goodwood — but trainer John Gallagher is 0/9 in the last 14 days, which tempers confidence despite the strong profile; needs the pace to lift to make her late run meaningful.
runners_data.comment: A winner four starts back, though that has been followed by two sevenths on the bounce, one of them last time out. Has run over today's trip and going before, but sits down among the makeweights on our figures here.

runners_data.name: Queen's Reign
runners_data.note: Hold-up type stepping back to 7f after two outings over a mile-plus at Nottingham and Sandown on softer ground; the 97-day absence is a concern, her sim-going record is modest (6/15), and she has a headgear flag (p) — connections appear to be freshening her for a Goodwood return but she needs everything to fall right.
runners_data.comment: Runner-up two starts back, and third three starts back, but sixth last time out and 97 days off since. Still without a win in her last five starts, leaving plenty to prove on her return.

runners_data.name: Radiant Beauty
runners_data.note: James Owen's mare is a natural front-runner or prominent racer whose last three wins have come over a mile at Goodwood — stepping back to 7f is interesting but she has been pushed to midfield on the map because prominent berths are already taken; her best form is over longer and she may not find enough speed to access her favoured position.
runners_data.comment: Won last time out, and again three starts back, for two wins in her last five starts. Yet she's only twelfth of fourteen on our figures, making those recent efforts hard to fully trust here.

runners_data.name: Sayidah Dariyan
runners_data.note: Ryan Moore rides the highest-rated prominently-placed runner aside from Flora Of Bermuda, but all five recent form runs are over 5-6f and this is a step up in trip; if she handles 7f, her class makes her dangerous from a handy position, though the strong sim-going record (8/11) is over shorter distances.
runners_data.comment: A below-par ninth last time out is easily forgiven given a win five starts back and a smart speed figure of 106. Rated second of fourteen, she has real scope to trouble the top-rated runner, with the patchy recent record the obvious caveat.

runners_data.name: Awaken
runners_data.note: George Boughey's three-year-old is a genuine pace-pressing type who has been pushed into the midfield map because the prominent slots are oversubscribed — her last two runs are zeros (0,0) on form, the 40-day break may help, but she has not fired at Goodwood; the redistribution understates her true running style but her current form makes the positional disadvantage academic.
runners_data.comment: A win five starts back is the standout, but that's since been followed by two unplaced efforts, including last time out. Has run over today's trip and going before, and sits mid-pack on our figures, leaving her capable of better than recent form suggests.

runners_data.name: Golden Palace
runners_data.note: Fahey's three-year-old has course form and a prominent running style, but her recent form is unremarkable (65-738) and the T14 strike rate is 1/40 — she is a natural pace-pressure type who simply cannot get to the front in this field; the positional squeeze hurts a runner already short on class.
runners_data.comment: Eighth last time out, third two starts back, but still without a win in her last five starts. Has run over today's trip and going before from draw 11, and ranks fifth of fourteen on our figures.

runners_data.name: Isle Of Fernandez
runners_data.note: Kevin Ryan's three-year-old has never run on Good ground at Goodwood — all recent form is on Soft — and the 80-day absence combined with a 0/8 sim-going record is a significant question mark; prominent in style but out of his comfort zone on this surface and likely facing a stiffer test than his form profile suggests.
runners_data.comment: A win five starts back and two subsequent thirds underline some ability, but she was below-par when eighth last time out and returns now from an 80-day absence. Rated ninth of fourteen on our figures, she's up against it in this company.

runners_data.name: Orion's Belt
runners_data.note: Returning from 305 days off for Richard Hannon, who has 9/49 in the T14 window — the layoff is the single biggest concern here, though his form before the break showed real promise with wins and places over course and trip; the redistribution to midfield masks a horse who would naturally want to press the pace, and rustiness after nearly a year off will be the deciding factor.
runners_data.comment: A win five starts back, and a runner-up two starts back, show ability, but she was below-par when ninth last time out and returns from a 305-day absence. Rated seventh of fourteen, hard to trust off such a lengthy gap.

runners_data.name: Planet Seeker
runners_data.note: Ralph Beckett's three-year-old is lightly raced and progressive, winning twice in four career starts including over this course and trip — Jamie Spencer rides, which suits a patient approach, but this horse's natural style is prominent and it has been pushed to midfield by weight of numbers; the combination of course-and-distance form and an upward trajectory makes it one to watch despite the positional compromise.
runners_data.comment: Won last time out, and again four starts back, for two wins in her last four starts - solid recent form. Yet she's only rated tenth of fourteen, meaning that improvement may not be enough to trouble this field's leaders.

runners_data.name: Zanthos
runners_data.note: Oisin Murphy partners the joint top-rated three-year-old, who won a Listed race over this trip at Goodwood last season and has run well from a prominent position throughout — the headgear flag (t) and a moderate recent run (9th in the Stewards' Cup) create a small question, but course and trip familiarity plus a trainer (Crisford) who spots opportunities are strong positives.
runners_data.comment: Two wins in her last five starts, one three starts back, and another five starts back, make her a serious threat on our figures. The recent dip - unplaced last time out and ninth before that - is the knock against her, but the deeper form is smart.

races.paceDynamic: Flora Of Bermuda is the one confirmed front-runner here, but she is a genuine 6f specialist stepping to 7f at Goodwood — she will likely dictate on a flat, even gallop rather than setting a scorching pace, meaning this shapes up as a steadily-run race with a single horse in control. Sayidah Dariyan, Dash Of Azure and Royal Velvet are the natural prominent types who should follow her through, with the pace distribution behind controlled and ungrouped. Several runners — Awaken, Golden Palace, Orion's Belt, Planet Seeker and Radiant Beauty — are genuinely prominent or front-running types in their natural form but cannot all secure that position in a field this size and have been mapped to midfield accordingly; of those, Dash Of Azure and Royal Velvet are best placed to actually sit close to the pace given their consistent near-front positioning at Goodwood. The tactical verdict is clear: this race shape strongly favours horses who can race prominently in the first four, absorb the moderate pace and quicken from two furlongs out — a stamina-test finish is unlikely; instead, a well-judged prominent run or a powerful mid-race move from just off the pace will be decisive.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Prominent Types Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If Flora Of Bermuda controls an honest but uncontested gallop and the race is won from the front three or four.
scenarios.body: Flora Of Bermuda sets a controlled tempo through the first half of the race, allowing Dash Of Azure, Royal Velvet and Sayidah Dariyan to travel sweetly in her wake before the race ignites at the two-furlong pole; horses with strong Goodwood form and an ability to quicken from a handy position are directly rewarded by this shape.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Late Pace Collapse
scenarios.trigger: If the moderate pace allows prominent types to quicken early, stringing the field out and leaving hold-up runners with too much ground to make up.
scenarios.body: Flora Of Bermuda's measured tempo means the leaders never really come back to the field, and quality Goodwood performers with tactical speed running prominently pull clear before the genuine hold-up horses can land their challenges; runners with proven course form who track the pace without being drawn into a flat-out effort early are the primary beneficiaries.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Find Late Gap
scenarios.trigger: If the pace quickens sharply enough mid-race to string the field and open ground for horses tracking from off the pace.
scenarios.body: A strong move from the two-furlong mark compresses energy expenditure in the pack, leaving Havana Pusey or Queen's Reign — genuine hold-up types who know this track well — with a clear lane to finish powerfully through beaten horses; this scenario needs the pace to be genuinely testing rather than pedestrian, which is against the grain of this race shape.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Front Runner Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Flora Of Bermuda is allowed to bowl along in front completely unchallenged at a canter and the prominent challengers are never close enough to reel her in.
scenarios.body: A complete lack of pressure turns this into a tactical exercise that suits a horse happy to roll on uncontested, and Flora Of Bermuda's class and course form — a winner over course and distance — makes her dangerous if rivals fail to read the race in time; however, her 6f preference and the calibre of the prominent types behind make this the least probable outcome.

watchPoints.text: Flora Of Bermuda's jockey James Doyle has a 6f specialist over 7f — watch whether she is allowed to coast in front or if Buick on Royal Velvet applies early pressure, because any increase in tempo from the front two would significantly alter the race shape.

Orion's Belt is returning from 305 days off and is a true prominent racer who could not get his natural position even if fully fit — watch for signs of sluggishness out of the stalls that confirm the layoff has dulled his early speed.

Planet Seeker, Awaken and Golden Palace are all genuine pace types compressed into midfield — if they push forward from wide draws regardless, they could create a scrappy, bunched mid-race pattern that turns the race into a lottery rather than a tactical test.

Queen's Reign's headgear flag and 97-day absence mean her starting price may be generous or a warning sign — watch for any market drift or late jockey booking changes, as connections appear to be pitching her fresh into a Group 3 off a long break.

Havana Pusey has the best strike rate of any horse in this field at Goodwood on Good ground over 7f (3W in 5) but her trainer Gallagher is 0/9 in the last 14 days — monitor whether the booking of Clifford Lee and any market moves suggest the yard believes this conditions suit before committing to her hold-up chance.

races.name: Veuve Clicquot Molecomb Stakes (Group 3)

runners_data.name: Adonius
runners_data.note: Three from three with all wins at 5f, including at Goodwood, and his sim-going record of 1/3 on comparable ground is solid; races prominently and is well-placed to track Hell Of A Spin from a handy pitch — Rebecca Menzies' yard has a live traveller at 84 days since last run, and no headgear concerns.
runners_data.comment: Three wins in his last three starts is about as strong a recent record as you'll find, form good enough to be rated third in this field. The one concern is a lengthy 84-day absence, but that unbeaten sequence makes him hard to leave out of the reckoning.

runners_data.name: Bill The Bull
runners_data.note: Recent form shows 12th and 8th at Goodwood in his last two, and despite being a genuine prominent type, he is carrying that style into a field with no space for him up front — the style fit penalty (0.92) is a real discount, and Adam Kirby only trains this runner (0/10 in 14 days is a concern).
runners_data.comment: A win three starts back stands out in an otherwise workmanlike record, backed up by a third five starts back. Quick to reappear 11 days after an unplaced run last time out, and rated sixth of eleven, he looks more a frame contender than a winner.

runners_data.name: El Floridita
runners_data.note: Last-time-out second at Goodwood over this exact course and distance, with a win here before that — his sim-going record reads 3 from 3 and he is one of the better-credentialed horses for this track; Rowan Scott takes over in the saddle and Nigel Tinkler's 14-day strike rate (2/23) is modest but the horse's Goodwood profile compensates.
runners_data.comment: Runner-up last time out, following a win two starts back, form strong enough to be rated fourth in this field. Has run over today's trip before, and with a fifth three starts back his only blemish, he's a leading threat throughout.

runners_data.name: Flight Signal
runners_data.note: Won impressively over this course and distance last time but is a natural prominent type who will find space at a premium here; the style fit flag (0.93) reflects the practical difficulty of him getting his favoured spot in a race already dominated by Hell Of A Spin, and Tom Marquand will need a clean draw and early speed to get into position.
runners_data.comment: A win two starts back is the highlight, but that was followed by an unplaced effort last time out, and he's rated bottom of this field - some way below his official mark. Has run over today's trip before, but there's plenty to prove against this line-up.

runners_data.name: Hell Of A Spin
runners_data.note: The race's lone front-runner with a Goodwood 5f win on her CV and a recent run just 18 days ago keeping her sharp; Adrian Keatley's 14-day form (3/14) is encouraging and she is the key pace reference — if she bowls along unchallenged, her ability to control the tempo makes her a central figure regardless of her modest OR of 79.
runners_data.comment: Won last time out, following a runner-up effort the time before, for a tidy recent record. Has run over today's trip and going before, but he's only rated ninth of eleven, leaving him plenty to find against a stronger level of rival.

runners_data.name: Ruler's Pride
runners_data.note: The field's only genuine hold-up runner, landing his 5f Goodwood win last time out under James Doyle — a powerful booking — but in a race with a lone front-runner and a compressed prominent group, he will need a stronger-than-expected tempo to pick them up; his sim-going record (2/2) is encouraging.
runners_data.comment: A win two starts back was followed by an unplaced effort last time out, and he's now rated tenth of eleven on our figures - some way below his official mark. Has run over today's trip before, but there's plenty of work to do against this field.

runners_data.name: Sale Shark
runners_data.note: Won at 5f on Good ground earlier in the career but his last two runs at 6f Goodwood have produced 5ths; Hugo Palmer's 14-day record (3/21) is acceptable, but like several others here, he is a true prominent type who will be racing out of that role, and the style fit discount (0.90) reflects a genuine positional problem.
runners_data.comment: A win three starts back has been followed by back-to-back fifths, the latest just 12 days ago. Has run over today's trip before, and rated fifth of eleven on our figures, he sits right in the mix for this contest.

runners_data.name: Undercover Affair
runners_data.note: Billy Loughnane rides a consistent type with multiple placed efforts at 5f Goodwood, but she has been redistributed to a hold-up position that is not her natural home (style fit 0.80) — her form actually reads as a handy, front-foot runner, and the further back she is forced to race, the more that consistent placed record is undermined.
runners_data.comment: Won last time out for his second success in his last six starts, with three more placed efforts underlining consistency. Has run over today's trip and going before, and rated seventh of eleven, he's competitive without being the biggest threat.

runners_data.name: Brazilian Diva
runners_data.note: Placed at Goodwood last time over this trip for the small Diego Dias yard (0/3 in 14 days), and while the form is honest, she is another horse whose prominent racing style will be compromised by the crowded pace group — Diego Lima takes the mount but the redistribution (style fit 0.92) is a meaningful structural hurdle.
runners_data.comment: Runner-up last time out, following a win two starts back, shows she retains ability, though a seventh and a fifth further back temper the claims. Has run over today's trip and going before, and rated eighth of eleven, she's workmanlike rather than an obvious threat.

runners_data.name: Crownbreaker
runners_data.note: Last-time-out winner at 5f on Soft for Kevin Philippart De Foy, who has a strong 14-day record (3/10); OR 97 gives him the class edge and David Egan is a key booking — his sim-going record on Good (3/4, 0W2P) suggests he handles the surface but has yet to win on it, something worth noting at the top of the market.
runners_data.comment: Won last time out, with a runner-up effort three starts back further boosting a smart recent record. The one blemish is a fifth two starts back, but she's rated second in this field and a big danger to the top-rated runner.

runners_data.name: Pershaada
runners_data.note: Richard Hannon sends out a filly with a win and two places at 5f, and Sean Levey's booking is significant given Hannon's volume (9/49 in 14 days); sim-going record is 2/4 with one win, and her form over this course at Goodwood is encouraging — she is one of the less compromised prominent types in the field and has a clear path to a forward pitch.
runners_data.comment: A win two starts back, backed up by a runner-up three starts back, underlines solid recent form, and she tops this field on our figures. The one blemish is a below-par fourth last time out, but the deeper form makes her the one to beat.

races.paceDynamic: Hell Of A Spin is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with only one genuine lead horse in an 11-runner field, she is highly likely to dictate an unchallenged, even gallop from the front — setting a fair but not scorching pace through Goodwood's sharp 5f. The field is overloaded with prominent types: Flight Signal, Bill The Bull, Sale Shark, Brazilian Diva and Undercover Affair are all natural forwardly-placed runners, but they cannot all occupy that space, meaning several will be squeezed into unfamiliar midfield berths where their style fit is compromised. El Floridita, Adonius and Crownbreaker are the prominent horses best placed to secure a genuine pitch just off the pace, while Ruler's Pride is the only true hold-up runner in the field. A solo front-runner setting a controlled, fair pace on Good turf over a flat 5f strongly favours horses who race prominently and can challenge from just off the leader in the straight — sit-and-sprint closers will have too little ground to make up.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Pace, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Hell Of A Spin leads at a fair, uncontested gallop and the race is decided by those tracking her in the first two or three positions.
scenarios.body: Hell Of A Spin sets a manageable tempo and the race unfolds as a sustained sprint from the 2f pole, rewarding horses who have tracked her and can quicken off a true pace; El Floridita and Adonius are ideally suited, with both holding Goodwood form and proven ability to travel prominently before asserting.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Front Runner Holds
scenarios.trigger: If the surrounding prominent horses jostle for position early and burn energy, leaving Hell Of A Spin to bowl along in front and simply outstay a disorganised field.
scenarios.body: The scrimmaging behind her allows Hell Of A Spin to lob along in a rhythm and build a lead that proves decisive on Good ground over this flat 5f; her trainer form (3/14 in 14 days) and unbeaten Goodwood win give this genuine credence even at OR 79.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Strong Gallop, Class Prevails
scenarios.trigger: If Hell Of A Spin is pressed earlier than expected and the pace quickens materially through the first two furlongs, stretching the field and setting up a class-driven finish.
scenarios.body: A stronger tempo tests stamina reserves and lifts the ceiling for the highest-rated runners who can travel smoothly before producing a decisive burst; Crownbreaker (OR 97, last-time-out winner) and Pershaada (OR 96, placed at Group level) have the class ceiling to capitalise when the race is run at a stiffer tempo.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Lands Late
scenarios.trigger: If pace is fierce enough and the field compact enough that Ruler's Pride, as the sole genuine hold-up type, arrives from the rear to finish over tired rivals.
scenarios.body: Ruler's Pride is the only horse with a true off-the-pace profile and James Doyle would need the race to be run at a flat-out gallop that ties up the principals; the scenario is structurally unlikely given a lone front-runner and few genuine closers, but Ruler's Pride's last-time-out 5f Goodwood win at OR 93 means this cannot be entirely dismissed.

watchPoints.text: Hell Of A Spin leads this field uncontested — watch whether any of the crowded prominent group (Flight Signal, El Floridita, Adonius) press her early, as the level of pressure she faces in the first furlong will define whether the race is truly run to suit front-runners or midfield challengers.

Flight Signal and Sale Shark both carry style-fit penalties and are genuine prominent types mapped out of role — watch for traffic issues and slow starts from either, as both need a clean break to have any realistic chance of recovering their natural position.

Ruler's Pride is James Doyle's sole hold-up runner and will need the pace to be materially stronger than a solo Hell Of A Spin is likely to set — watch the sectionals through the first two furlongs to judge whether he has any realistic chance of arriving late.

Crownbreaker's last win came on Soft ground and his Goodwood record on Good is placed-only (0W2P in sim-going) — watch whether he travels as fluently here as he did at Nottingham last time, as his winning profile may be more ground-dependent than his OR suggests.

Undercover Affair has been redistributed to a rear position that is not her natural style — watch how Billy Loughnane handles the first furlong, as if she is allowed to stride forward naturally she could emerge as a much bigger factor than her positional mapping implies.

races.name: Visit Qatar Sussex Stakes (Group 1)

runners_data.name: Docklands
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up horse for Harry Eustace and James Doyle with a win and three places from five outings at Goodwood on Good ground; 18 days since his last run is ideal freshness, and his strong course-specific record makes him one of the primary beneficiaries if the pace shapes up to suit late runners.
runners_data.comment: Docklands was sixth last time out but a winner four starts back, and he has run over today's trip and going before. Rated 124 and ranked fifth of twelve, he's competitive without standing out.

runners_data.name: Lake Forest
runners_data.note: William Haggas's five-year-old ran just yesterday which flags as a significant freshness concern despite impressive course form including a recent win at Goodwood over 7f on Good; Cieren Fallon will look to track Bow Echo prominently, and a repeat of his best form would make him extremely competitive.
runners_data.comment: Lake Forest won last time out and was also successful three starts back, dips to fifth and seventh the only blemish. Rated 128, the main concern is the quick turnaround after running just a day ago.

runners_data.name: Never So Brave
runners_data.note: Andrew Balding's five-year-old is in fine heart with four wins from his last nine starts, but his naturally prominent racing style means he is almost certain to be denied his preferred slot in this traffic-heavy race, reducing his win chance in this specific race shape even if his ability on Good ground at Goodwood is not in question.
runners_data.comment: Never So Brave rebounded to be runner-up last time out following two fifths and a seventh, with a win five starts back among his form. Rated 116 and ranked seventh of twelve, he has claims but sits behind more consistent types.

runners_data.name: Opera Ballo
runners_data.note: Charlie Appleby's four-year-old has won five of his last ten and carries the highest OR in the field at 125, making him the standout on class; William Buick will seek a handy prominent position which is his natural home, and his consistent winning record specifically at Goodwood on Good ground makes this course-and-conditions profile highly appealing.
runners_data.comment: Opera Ballo was third last time out but is a treble winner across his previous three starts, and has run over today's trip and going before. Rated 126 and ranked third of twelve, the 43-day absence since his last run is the main query.

runners_data.name: Qirat
runners_data.note: Ralph Beckett's five-year-old is a natural pace-rider who will struggle to secure his preferred prominent berth with so many similar types in this field; his Good-ground Goodwood form is solid including a recent win over 7f here, but being shuffled back in the order undercuts his chance.
runners_data.comment: Qirat was fourth last time out but a winner two starts back, with a seventh and an unplaced run further back the blots. Rated 116 and ranked eighth of twelve, he's back quickly after running just a day ago.

runners_data.name: Seagulls Eleven
runners_data.note: Oisin Murphy partners this Hugo Palmer four-year-old who has shown very strong form at Goodwood, winning twice on Good and Soft and placing on his most recent run over this course and trip; as a genuine hold-up horse he is not affected by the traffic battle for position early and could pick up a rewarding late run if the pace is true.
runners_data.comment: Third last time out, with wins two and three starts back, yet ranks only tenth of twelve on our figures. He needs to find more to trouble this field, though an 18-day break should have him fresh.

runners_data.name: Ten Bob Tony
runners_data.note: Ed Walker's five-year-old has back-to-back wins most recently but a 43-day absence and his preferred front-end style working against him here; with Bow Echo almost certain to dominate the lead, Ten Bob Tony will be forced to sit in unfamiliar company for much of the race which tempers confidence despite his recent course-winning form.
runners_data.comment: Ten Bob Tony won last time out and was also successful two starts back, though a below-par eighth sandwiched among his last five starts is a blot. Rated 123 and ranked sixth of twelve, the 43-day gap since his latest run is a query.

runners_data.name: Bow Echo
runners_data.note: George Boughey's unbeaten three-year-old has won all five starts at Goodwood over this exact trip on Good ground, making his pace-setting role here a natural extension of his entire racing pattern; Billy Loughnane will fire him to the front immediately, and the key question is whether his front-running supremacy extends to this calibre of Group 1 opposition.
runners_data.comment: Bow Echo has won all five of his starts and has run over today's trip and going before, a rare picture of consistency for this level. Rated 128, the only slight query is the 43-day break since his last outing.

runners_data.name: Dorset
runners_data.note: Aidan O'Brien's three-year-old has a modest recent record with form figures of 4-7-8-9 in his last four runs and is another natural prominently-positioned racer who will be squeezed out of his preferred spot by this competitive prominent contingent; Wayne Lordan faces a difficult tactical problem and the OR of 103 looks light in this company.
runners_data.comment: Dorset rallied to fourth last time out after finishing ninth, eighth and seventh in between, with his only win coming five starts back. Rated 111 and ranked eleventh of twelve, he has plenty to find, though a quick 10-day turnaround keeps him fresh.

runners_data.name: Gstaad
runners_data.note: Ryan Moore on an O'Brien three-year-old who has been consistently placed over Goodwood's mile on Good ground, finishing second three times at the course with a win sandwiched in; his prominent style is genuinely suited to tracking Bow Echo, and Moore's tactical intelligence will be crucial in finding the right position in what will be a congested mid-division.
runners_data.comment: Gstaad has been placed in all five of his recent starts, winning twice and finishing runner-up in the rest. Rated 126 and ranked fourth of twelve, the main concern is the 43-day break since he last ran.

runners_data.name: Puerto Rico
runners_data.note: Christophe Soumillon takes over on this O'Brien three-year-old whose form has dropped sharply with finishing positions of 4th and 6th in his last two; a prominent racer by nature who will be pushed into the mid-division pack, his style fit is compromised in this shape and his declining form line adds further concern even with a top jockey aboard.
runners_data.comment: Puerto Rico won three in a row further back but has since faded to fourth and sixth in his last two starts, ranking bottom of twelve at 105. A 43-day break offers hope of a bounce, but he needs to rediscover that form.

runners_data.name: Zavateri
runners_data.note: Eve Johnson Houghton's three-year-old is unbeaten in three Goodwood starts all on Good ground and Charles Bishop has ridden him to win twice at the track; the 102-day absence since his last run is the outstanding concern, and while his course record is eye-catching, ring-rustiness against this calibre of Group 1 rivals is a genuine risk.
runners_data.comment: Zavateri strung together three wins further back and was runner-up last time out, sandwiched around a fourth two starts back, and ranks ninth of twelve at 116. His main obstacle is a lengthy 102-day absence since that effort.

races.paceDynamic: Bow Echo is the one confirmed front-runner here and, crucially, he is unbeaten in five starts all at Goodwood over this exact trip — he will stride straight to the front and attempt to control the race from the outset. With no genuine rival willing to take him on for the lead, he should find a comfortable, measured gallop that does not burn his petrol early, making this a truly-run mile rather than a falsely fast one. The field carries far more prominent types than the race shape can accommodate: Puerto Rico, Never So Brave, Ten Bob Tony, Dorset and Qirat are all natural pace-riders who will be shuffled into mid-division behind Bow Echo and Lake Forest, creating a bunched, tactical contest rather than a strung-out affair. That dynamic — a single controlled pace-setter dictating a steady fractions race — strongly favours the horse who can quicken from a handy position in the straight, benefiting genuine prominent racers like Opera Ballo and Gstaad who have the class and finishing kick to pounce once Bow Echo's controlled lead is challenged off the final bend.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Bow Echo Controls, Class Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If Bow Echo dictates an honest but not suicidal gallop and the prominent class horses are close enough to strike turning for home.
scenarios.body: Bow Echo sets a smooth tempo from the front while Opera Ballo and Gstaad track him in a handy position, both with the scope to quicken when the race ignites inside the final two furlongs; a single front-runner setting a fair pace is the optimum setup for a high-class hold-up or prominent horse to find a clear run and produce a late sectional.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Bow Echo Wins Wire-To-Wire
scenarios.trigger: If Bow Echo's uncontested lead translates into an unbreakable rhythm and his rivals leave their runs too late in a slowly-run mile.
scenarios.body: With no rival willing to commit to pressing Bow Echo, the pace could be sufficiently controlled that he never truly ties up, keeping a length or two in hand as the field spreads wide in the straight; his five-from-five record at this course and distance, all on Good ground, underscores that this is not fantasy — he is exceptionally well-suited to these specific conditions.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is fast enough to string the field out and a genuine hold-up runner finds a gap to come through the pack with a sustained run.
scenarios.body: Docklands and Seagulls Eleven are the true hold-up horses who will be sitting furthest back, and if the tempo is brisk enough to cause attrition near the front they have the ability to pick up momentum through beaten rivals; Docklands has winning form over this course and distance while Seagulls Eleven has shown strong form on Good ground at Goodwood, giving both a live chance if the race is truly truly run.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Scrambled Midfield, Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If the glut of redistributed prominent types cause interference, positional battles and traffic problems throughout the race.
scenarios.body: Puerto Rico, Never So Brave, Ten Bob Tony and Dorset are all naturally prominent horses jammed into a false midfield position; if several of them push forward aggressively in the early stages it could create a fractious, uneven gallop with bunching into the home straight, handing an advantage to any runner fortunate enough to find an unimpeded run wide of the melee.

watchPoints.text: Bow Echo — if Billy Loughnane pings him cleanly from the stalls and goes unchallenged to the front, watch whether he quickens the tempo entering the final quarter-mile, which would be the decisive tactical moment separating those with a winning chance from those left treading water.

Opera Ballo — William Buick will be aiming to sit just behind Bow Echo in second or third; if he gets that position cleanly, his class and course form make him the most dangerous individual in the race and any early bump or traffic issue that delays his tracking move would be critical.

Lake Forest — the one-day gap between his last run and today is unusually short and should be monitored closely; if he runs below his Goodwood benchmark it may be fatigue rather than form, and backers should note the recency flag is a genuine concern not a scheduling quirk.

Puerto Rico, Never So Brave, Ten Bob Tony — all three will attempt to push forward in the early stages and create a compressing effect behind Bow Echo; watch the first furlong for any jostling between them as a scramble for position could cause interference that disrupts runners attempting to track the pace cleanly.

Zavateri — 102 days off the track is a long absence for a three-year-old in a Group 1, and while his all-Good Goodwood record is flawless, Charles Bishop will need to manage his freshness carefully; if he shows any signs of being on his toes in the preliminaries that would be an early signal he may not be fully wound up for a maximum effort.

races.name: Coral Charlton Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Expert Agent
runners_data.note: Six career runs at Goodwood over 6f with a win and two places here; settled prominent suits this shape perfectly, and 11 days since last run is fresh enough under Marco Ghiani for a yard in fine current form (4/31 T14).
runners_data.comment: Ranked second of 28 on our figures, Expert Agent has a winner three starts back, and again five starts back, among two wins in its last six starts. Only a modest fourth last time out, 11 days ago, is the concern.

runners_data.name: Sir Garfield
runners_data.note: The confirmed lone front runner; gets a dream solo lead on good ground with Jason Hart and has won twice here at this trip, though his STYLE_FIT flag notes he is catalogued as P rather than pure L — his natural role is entirely appropriate here and his 10/15 good-going sim record reinforces viability.
runners_data.comment: Won two starts back, and again three back, though sixth last time out and seventh four starts back temper the case. Fit again 12 days on with experience of today's trip, but only 16th of 28 on our figures.

runners_data.name: Mythical Composer
runners_data.note: 175 days off the track is the dominant concern; prominent style suits the race shape but the fitness query on a return from a lengthy break for Clive Cox is hard to ignore, headgear (p) suggests he needs it.
runners_data.comment: One win in its last five starts, coming two starts back, with fourth the finish on each of the other four occasions. Ranked fourth of 28 on our figures with experience of today's trip, but a 175-day absence since is the concern.

runners_data.name: Winchurch
runners_data.note: True hold-up horse who has won twice at Goodwood over sprint trips on good ground; Mason Paetel's 5lb claim helps offset 137lbs and a 27-day break, and he is best served by a fast-run race that the sole front runner may not deliver.
runners_data.comment: Three wins in its last six starts, the latest coming last time out, though the yard is out of form (1/23, 4% in the last 14 days). That leaves it only 21st of 28 on our figures, despite already having run over today's trip.

runners_data.name: Lipsink
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old veteran whose prominent style and course record (1W4P from 8 sim-going runs) makes him a natural fit here; 47 days between runs for Michael Appleby's yard, which has a low recent strike rate (1/24 T14), is the question mark.
runners_data.comment: Three wins in its last five starts, second last time out, and the yard is out of form (1/23, 4% in the last 14 days). Ranked 19th of 28 on our figures after a 47-day layoff, with experience of today's trip.

runners_data.name: Under The Twilight
runners_data.note: Won here over this exact course and distance on good ground recently; two further Goodwood places at 6f underline course affinity, and the prominent style lands perfectly in this controlled-pace shape under Harry Davies.
runners_data.comment: A winner last time out but modest form before that (fourth, fourth and second across her previous three), fit again 16 days on. Rated seventh of 28 on our figures, with experience of today's trip.

runners_data.name: Supreme King
runners_data.note: Three consecutive Goodwood places including two seconds at 6f and 7f; OR 78 with Oisin Murphy booked is significant, and his prominent style means he settles beautifully off Sir Garfield — limited good-ground sim (3/15) slightly tempers enthusiasm.
runners_data.comment: Second in each of its last three starts, with a solitary win four starts back its only success among its last six. Ranked ninth of 28 on our figures after a 19-day break, with experience of today's trip.

runners_data.name: Mae Amor
runners_data.note: Hold-up mare who wears a visor; won here over 6f on good ground but her last two Goodwood starts produced a 6th and 9th, and the field's congested midfield may leave David Allan with nowhere to go until very late.
runners_data.comment: Well beaten in each of her last two starts (sixth, then ninth), with just one win in her last five, four starts back. Ranked 22nd of 28 on our figures, though she does have experience of today's trip.

runners_data.name: Vingegaard
runners_data.note: Won at Goodwood over 6f last time, returning from 43 days off with a tongue tie; Ryan Sexton rides and the hold-up style means he needs something to go wrong in front — feasible if the prominent runners jam up.
runners_data.comment: Fit again after a 43-day break, having won last time out, though the form before that is moderate — sixth and third, then three more modest efforts. Ranked 12th of 28 on our figures, with experience of today's trip.

runners_data.name: Cashbox
runners_data.note: OR 80 three-year-old with a blinker; two wins already at 7f on this ground for Charles Hills/David Egan, but coming back to 6f after three successive 7f runs at Goodwood raises a small trip query, though his prominent style suits the shape.
runners_data.comment: Second last time out, seventh two starts back, but a winner four and five starts back. Ranked 17th of 28 on our figures, with experience of today's trip from draw 26.

runners_data.name: Charlie Mason
runners_data.note: Tony Carroll's 5-year-old is a genuine front-runner type whose Goodwood record is modest (8th and 6th in last two here); with the field carrying far more prominent horses than the pace can accommodate, he is among those most likely to get bumped back from his natural berth despite a win on soft ground 15 days ago.
runners_data.comment: Tops our figures on 89 and fit again 15 days on, with a win three starts back the standout form. The concern is a run of modest efforts either side of it — eighth, sixth and two sevenths.

runners_data.name: Wreck It Ryley
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with a visor; recent form string is uninspiring (483896) and a 9th at Goodwood last time out over 6f on good ground is the most relevant data point — needs significant improvement.
runners_data.comment: Yet to win in its last six starts, with only a third four starts back standing out from a run of sixth, ninth and eighth-place efforts. Ranked 20th of 28 on our figures, though it does have experience of today's trip.

runners_data.name: Born Slippy
runners_data.note: 298 days off the track for a 3-year-old makes this highly speculative regardless of a previous Goodwood placing; prominent style would suit the shape if fit but the layoff is a near-disqualifying concern for Saffie Osborne.
runners_data.comment: A third two starts back, and a winner four starts back, give it the form to fancy for today. It's our selection, with the one blot a below-par eighth last time out before a 298-day absence since.

runners_data.name: Arduis Invicta
runners_data.note: Hold-up 3-year-old whose recent Goodwood form over sprint trips is encouraging (4th, 2nd); Tom Eaves knows this track well and the horse is stepping up in trip experience gradually — needs a stronger gallop than one lone front runner is likely to provide.
runners_data.comment: Ranked third of 28 on our figures and fourth last time out having been runner-up two starts back, she looks capable of running well again. Still without a win in her last five starts is the one knock against her.

runners_data.name: Silver Wraith
runners_data.note: Has run four times at Goodwood over this trip winning once and placing twice — strong course affinity; however, this is a genuinely prominent-natured horse that the crowded pace positions may force to settle deeper than ideal under Sean Levey, tempering confidence despite the course credentials.
runners_data.comment: Runner-up last time out just six days ago, quick to back up a campaign that also included a win five starts back, and another second four starts back. Ranked 13th of 28 on our figures, with experience of today's trip.

runners_data.name: Rory Rocket
runners_data.note: Three wins at Goodwood over 6f is a striking record; although mapped to midfield due to redistribution pressure, his true running style sits closer to hold-up, and Jude Fernandes (7) claims 7lbs — the style-fit tag (0.93) warns he may be racing out of role in this controlled-pace scenario.
runners_data.comment: Rory Rocket has three wins in its last six starts and was third most recently, yet our figures rank it only 26th of 28 despite that record. It has experience of today's trip, though finding this company too sharp looks the risk.

races.paceDynamic: Sir Garfield is the confirmed front runner and, with only one genuine pace-setter across 28 runners, this race will be run at a controlled, honest-but-sustainable gallop from the off rather than a truly contested early pace. Sir Garfield will stride into a clear lead down the Goodwood straight, setting a rhythm that suits horses who can travel prominently off a single pace and pick up in the final furlong — Expert Agent, Lipsink, Under The Twilight and Supreme King are the natural beneficiaries of that position. Good ground throughout the card confirms a true surface that will not blunt acceleration and slightly rewards those with tactical speed close to the pace rather than those needing the race to fall apart late. The field carries a significant excess of prominent-running types — Kanishka, Riley Rocks, French Affair, Sargent Dennis, Ziggy's Condor and Charlie Mason are all true prominent racers who cannot all secure their favoured position, meaning several will be shuffled back against their will, diluting the hold-up threat and concentrating race-winning advantage with the genuine, unfettered front-rank horses who land spot-on in this shape; on balance, the tactical verdict firmly favours genuine prominent racers who can settle just off Sir Garfield's controlled lead and pounce inside the final furlong.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Prominent types dominate
scenarios.trigger: If Sir Garfield bowls along at a fair but unhurried pace and the genuine prominent racers lock in directly behind him.
scenarios.body: Sir Garfield sets a controlled tempo and those immediately on his heels — Expert Agent, Under The Twilight, Supreme King and Lipsink — travel without expending energy fighting for position, giving them a decisive advantage when they kick from two furlongs out. Good ground means the pace is true enough to string the field out early, leaving late chargers with too much to make up.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Sir Garfield dictates and wins
scenarios.trigger: If Sir Garfield's single-runner pace proves genuinely unchallenged and the gap he builds proves insurmountable on a flat straight.
scenarios.body: With no horse to pressurise him at any stage, Sir Garfield controls every fraction and builds a lead that is never seriously threatened, his 10/15 good-ground sim record underpinning the fitness angle under Jason Hart. The prominent horses behind him find the gap too large to close when they finally quicken, and he holds on going away.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-up horses pounce late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace quickens sharply early enough to string out the field and create a genuine gap for the genuine hold-up horses to exploit in the final 100 yards.
scenarios.body: Winchurch, Vingegaard and Rory Rocket — true hold-up horses with legitimate course form — thread through late if Sir Garfield's unsupported lead over-promises and the prominent types hit a flat spot at the two-furlong pole. This scenario requires a faster-than-expected early pace and some scrimmaging among the over-loaded prominent brigade to cost them momentum, which is plausible but not likely given the single front runner.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Redistributed runners disrupt
scenarios.trigger: If several of the displaced prominent types push forward aggressively and turn the early stages into a contested scramble.
scenarios.body: Kanishka, French Affair and Riley Rocks refusing to settle wide or deep could inject unexpected pressure on Sir Garfield through the first two furlongs, collapsing the controlled tempo and turning this into a rough-and-tumble affair that produces a ragged, attritional finish. In that scenario horses with the most Goodwood course form and adaptability — Supreme King and Cashbox — benefit from possessing the tactical composure to survive the chaos.
